meta.title: The media shelf — quintessential reading & viewing
meta.note: Books, films, and papers that shaped the idea of virtual worlds. Shown on the shelf in the history station and as the reading list in #history.

items.title: True Names
items.creator: Vernor Vinge
items.blurb: The novella that saw it first: pseudonymous lives in a consensual imagined space, a decade before the web.

items.title: TRON
items.creator: Steven Lisberger
items.blurb: Inside the machine as a place — the aesthetic half the industry has been chasing ever since (this site included).

items.title: Neuromancer
items.creator: William Gibson
items.blurb: Coined cyberspace as a “consensual hallucination” — the word the whole field grew up inside.

items.title: The Lessons of Lucasfilm's Habitat
items.creator: Chip Morningstar & Randy Farmer
items.blurb: The field's founding postmortem: everything hard about running a world full of people, learned the first time.

items.title: Snow Crash
items.creator: Neal Stephenson
items.blurb: Named the Metaverse and the Street; half the companies on the map are trying to build this book.

items.title: Designing Virtual Worlds
items.creator: Richard Bartle
items.blurb: MUD1's co-creator writes the discipline down: the definitive text on what worlds are and who they're for.

items.title: Sword Art Online
items.creator: Reki Kawahara
items.blurb: The series that taught a generation (and half of VRChat) to want full-dive — the trapped-in-the-game story as aspiration.

items.title: Ready Player One
items.creator: Ernest Cline
items.blurb: The OASIS brought the metaverse back into boardrooms — nostalgia as world-engine, for better and worse.
